Likelihood profiles of effective doses, peak doses and benchmark doses

Source: R/profile.R
profile.edTMB.Rd

Profile likelihood of the estimates of ed, peak and bmd, used by confint(method="profile"); the result can be reused with confint and plotted.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'edTMB'
profile(
  fitted,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.99,
  maxit = 100,
  progress = interactive(),
  ...
)

Arguments

fitted

an edTMB object

parm

effective doses to profile, names or positions in coef(fitted); default all

level

the highest confidence level the profiles are computed for

maxit

maximum number of steps in each direction

progress

logical, show a progress bar over the profiled effective doses

...

ignored

Value

a profile.edTMB object, which has the confint and plot methods of profile.drmTMB

Details

Profiles the (marginal) log-likelihood for the effective doses. At each value of an effective dose, the model is reparameterised: the effective dose is a function of b3, b4 and b5 that can be solved for b4, so one coefficient of b4 is computed from the effective dose and the other coefficients, which are re-optimised.

The dose at the peak of a hormesis curve (peak) is profiled in the same way, as b4 follows from the peak dose and the other parameters; profiles are not available for the response at the peak.

The profiles are for the effective doses of the population curves, without the random effects; the variation between groups (random=TRUE in ed) and the residual variation are not included. For the models on the log-dose scale and the models without b3, the effective doses are profiled on the log scale. Gaussian and lognormal models with small-sample inference (without random effects, see drmTMBcontrol) use the F-based cutoff of profile.drmTMB.

Examples

mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
pe <- profile(ed(mod, respLev = c(10, 50)))
confint(pe)
#>            2.5 %   97.5 %
#> 10:lf1 0.9813209 1.774205
#> 50:lf1 2.8792091 3.703799
plot(pe)
